message.content: I'll raise cash on Pennsylvania Avenue first so the pinks can actually be housed.
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have a full pink monopoly with no houses. I can build on ST_CHARLES_PLACE, STATES_AVENUE, and VIRGINIA_AVENUE for $100 each. My cash is $376.

Even building requires one house on each pink property. That costs $300 and leaves $76. I cannot afford four houses without mortgaging. I am weighing whether to mortgage a property to build more.

Mortgaging four properties would raise cash to $786. That allows seven houses total, split 3-2-2 across the pink monopoly. The rent jump from three houses is large enough to justify the mortgage.

Opponent p2 has a dark blue monopoly with two houses on each property. Standard rent for Park Place is $500 and Boardwalk is $600. This makes the pink monopoly a strong defensive target.

p2 has three railroads and mortgaged utilities. With $195 cash, they need only $5 more to build a third house on the dark blues. That would raise rent to $1100 and $1400.

p3 has a full red monopoly with one house each on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Tennessee is mortgaged.

p3 also owns Baltic, Oriental, and Vermont. Connecticut blocks them from completing a light blue monopoly.

With $53 cash, p3 can mortgage Baltic, Oriental, and Vermont for roughly $130 more. That would let them build one additional house on the reds, raising rent to $270–$300 each.

p4 has $1081 and four properties but no monopolies.

p4 has a Get Out of Jail Free card and no monopolies. Unowned properties include Atlantic, Marvin Gardens, and Pacific.

The orange and brown monopolies are split between p4 and p3. The greens are split between p4, p3, and me.

Landing on Boardwalk would cost $600. That is more than my current cash of $376. I would go bankrupt or mortgage everything to survive.

I will mortgage Pennsylvania Avenue, B&O Railroad, and St. James Place for $350. That brings my cash to $726, enough to build seven houses evenly across the pink monopoly. I will leave $26 behind.

I am deciding which pink property gets three houses. Virginia Avenue has the highest rent at three houses, but St. Charles Place is a more frequent landing spot after Jail. I am weighing traffic frequency against rent potential.

I will place three houses on Virginia Avenue and two on the other pinks. I am also considering mortgaging Connecticut Avenue to block p3's light blue monopoly.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue will not transfer ownership, so p3 still cannot complete the light blue monopoly. B&O Railroad is worth mortgaging because p2 already owns three other railroads and the rent is only $25. Pennsylvania Avenue is also safe to mortgage; p4 would need Pacific to complete a greens set and has no incentive to buy it from me. I am now weighing whether the 3-2-2 house split justifies stripping all other assets.

I cannot mortgage the pink properties while they have houses. I am already bankrupted by dark blue rent unless I build. Seven houses will generate enough income to threaten opponents. Three houses on Virginia Avenue alone can bankrupt p3 and hurt p2.

A 3-2-2 house split is the only viable strategy. Building just one house on each pink property would leave me with only $76 and weak rent. Mortgage only Pennsylvania Avenue for five houses instead, and I would still have only $36 left. The jump from two to three houses is the critical threshold that makes the set dangerous.

I am now considering mortgaging Connecticut Avenue for an extra $60. That would raise my cash to about $86, giving me a small buffer against tax cards and small rent hits. Selling houses later would return only half their cost, so I want to avoid that pain if possible.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue adds $60 in cash but also 10% interest to unmortgage later. I will mortgage it for the extra buffer. Total cash becomes $786, allowing seven houses with $86 left over. Eight or nine houses are impossible with only $786.

I am now calculating the exact cash shortfall. p2's three railroads charge $100, which I cannot cover with only $86. Selling one house would return $50 and cover that rent. I still face a death trap from p2's dark blue properties.

I am considering trades before building. p4 could buy my PA or St James for monopolies, but selling those would help them while giving up blockers. I will not trade away any blocker properties. I also rejected trading with p3 because they own reds and I do not want to help them.

I will not give p2 my B&O Railroad. That would let them complete four railroads and collect $200 per landing. They already have $195, which is only $5 short of building a third house on the dark blues.

I cannot give p2 any cash. They already have enough to build a third house on one dark blue property and reach 3-2. I must mortgage and build immediately to stop them from escalating. I can only perform one action per turn.

The engine will ask again if more post-turn actions remain legal. I will mortgage properties first, then build houses, then end my turn. Three mortgages raise cash to $726, enough for seven houses with $26 left over. I am now deciding whether to mortgage Connecticut Avenue as a fourth action for an extra $60 buffer.

I will mortgage Connecticut Avenue for the extra $60 buffer. I am now weighing whether to build three houses first with my current cash and then mortgage and build more, since building rules allow multiple post-turn builds.

Mortgaging must precede building because seven houses cost $700. I will mortgage Pennsylvania Avenue first, then build all seven houses in one action. I will post a short confident public message. I am also checking whether p4's $1081 and current position on Chance create any reason to avoid the all-in 3-2-2 plan.

p3 is on New York Avenue and may land on my pink properties in a few turns. Two houses on States or Virginia would bankrupt p3 and remove the red threat. I also notice p2 is currently on Virginia Avenue, which is one of my properties.

I paid p2 $100 rent on Reading before turn 59. p2 is currently on Virginia Avenue. Building houses now will not retroactively charge rent for that landing.

The main risk of an all-in plan is bankruptcy to p2's dark blue properties. If I cannot pay, houses return to the bank and properties revert to p2. Building creates bankruptcy threats of my own. The player who builds wins.

I am behind on development. p2 has four houses on dark blues and p3 has three on reds, while I have none. I must catch up immediately.

The pink 3-2-2 plan is correct. My best rent is $500 versus their $600, but I have three properties instead of two, so I have more chances to hit. Red properties are also a threat to everyone.

I will decide which pink property gets three houses at build time. For this action, I will only mortgage.

I confirmed that the mortgage tool takes only a space key and lets the engine calculate the amount.

I will build seven houses with three on Virginia Avenue and two each on States and St. Charles Place, leaving $86 or $26 behind. I am now reconsidering whether to mortgage Connecticut Avenue; $86 is enough to survive most chance cards and taxes, while $26 would leave me defenseless against p2's $100 railroad rent.

I rejected selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p4. That would give p4 enough cash to buy Pacific and build hotels on the greens, threatening me with $1275-$1400 rent. I will mortgage only one property this turn.

I will not sell St. James Place to p4, because that would help them complete an orange monopoly and create a jail trap. I also rejected selling Connecticut Avenue to p3, since they could then build a cheap light blue set that would be difficult to pay off.

I am now weighing build order to maximize immediate threat. Virginia Avenue is the most expensive to develop, but it may be landed on more often than St. Charles Place. I will mortgage and build without trading.

Standard rent tables confirm Virginia Avenue's $500 three-house rent is the highest in the set. St. Charles Place and States Avenue would yield only $450 with three houses, so Virginia gets the full three-house stack.
